subject: Clarify how tokens are counted for system prompts, tool calls, and rounding
messages:

Subject: Quick clarifications on token counting and discounts

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile. Before we move to final commercial terms, procurement asked me to get precise answers on a few billing nuances so we can model monthly spend. I tried to summarize our typical usage and a few concrete questions below. Can you confirm?

Sample conversational flow (simplified):
- System prompt (server-side template): ~50 tokens (applied at session start)
- User message: 120 tokens
- Model emits a function call (tool call) to our retrieval adapter; the model emits ~40 tokens to form the JSON args (that shows up as the model output)
- Retrieval tool returns a 300-token document (not generated by Redwood model; returned by an external retrieval service)
- Model consumes that retrieval result in the next turn and emits 350 output tokens to the user

Questions:
1) How are these counted on the bill? Specifically: which pieces are "input" tokens vs "output" tokens? Does the JSON wrapper around the function call count as output?
2) For the retrieval tool response (300 tokens) — we pipeline it back into the model. Is that content billed as input tokens by Redwood when the model reconsumes it?
3) Do you apply any caching for the system prompt so repeated sessions with the same system message don't keep being billed? If so, how does caching affect counts?
4) Rounding/pricing detail: does Redwood round up token usage per-request to some bucket (e.g., nearest 10/100/1000) or do you sum exact tokens and then compute cost at invoice time? Also any quirks for streaming outputs (partial tokens emitted)?
5) Finally: do negotiated discounts on the rate card apply to all of the above usage (hosted model tokens) or are there exclusions (e.g., third-party plug-in calls or retrieval connector charges)?

If you can give an example cost calc with numbers (we can swap in real rates later), that would be ideal. Procurement also asked for a one-page note we can attach to the SOW that explains billing mechanics.

Thanks,
James

Hi James — great questions, thanks for the detailed sample flow. Looping in Monica (SE) and Karthik (pricing) to provide the mechanics and a short example calc. I'm attaching a draft rate card and a CSV with a few usage examples.

High-level answers up front:
- We bill based on actual token counts processed by Redwood models.
- Model-emitted function call JSON is counted as model output tokens.
- Any content fed back into the model (including tool responses you inject into the context) is counted as input tokens for the subsequent model turn.
- Rounding to currency (cents) happens at invoice time after summing all tokens; we do not perform a per-request rounding to large buckets.
- Negotiated discounts apply to Redwood-hosted model consumption (hosted API/Dedicated) only; third-party connector charges (if billed by the connector provider) are excluded unless listed on the SOW.

Karthik / Monica — can you validate the granular example below and confirm caching/streaming nuances?

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on token counting and discounts (detailed)

Diego / Monica — writing up the detailed mechanics so we have a single source of truth to send to Acme. I've kept the examples aligned with James' numbers.

Token accounting rules (hosted API):
- Input tokens: any text that is supplied to the model at a request boundary. This includes system prompts, user messages, and any tool responses or retrieved documents that you include in the model context for the next turn.
- Output tokens: any tokens emitted by the model as part of its response. This includes plain text and tokens that form a function call (i.e., the JSON arguments the model emits when making a tool call).
- Tool/plugin responses: content produced by an external retrieval system or plugin that is only returned to the client and not fed back into the model context is not billed as Redwood model input tokens. However, if you feed that retrieval text into the model (so the model consumes it), it becomes input tokens and is billed.
- Caching and prefix behavior:
  - Session-level system prompts: for hosted API, we perform short-term prefix caching of identical system messages per-client session (default TTL = 30 minutes). If the system prompt is identical and a cache hit occurs, we do not re-bill the cached tokens for each request; we only bill for the delta (the non-cached tokens).
  - Note: Dedicated and Private customers can opt into longer/advanced prefix caching policies (configurable) which further reduce billed input for repeated shared prefixes.
- Streaming: tokens emitted during streaming are counted as output tokens as they are generated. Billing uses integer token counts (there are no fractional tokens). If a stream is terminated early (user cancels), you are billed for the tokens actually emitted up to cancellation.
- Rounding/pricing math: we count tokens exactly (integer counts) and sum input and output tokens separately across the billing period. Pricing is applied to the summed token totals and the resulting dollar amount is rounded to cents for invoicing. We do NOT round up individual requests to artificial 1K buckets.

Concrete example using James' numbers (assume no prior cache hit for the session system prompt):
- Turn 1 (initial call):
  - Input tokens: system (50) + user (120) = 170 input tokens billed
  - Output tokens: model emits function-call JSON args (40) => 40 output tokens billed
  - Cost impact (per-turn): input 170, output 40
- External retrieval returns 300 tokens (retrieval service)
  - If you send that 300-token text back into the model as the next input, those 300 tokens are billed as input tokens on the following model call. If you do not feed it back into the model (client-only), Redwood does not bill those 300 tokens.
- Turn 2 (model consumes retrieval + responds):
  - Input tokens: system (if included in context; if cached we may only bill the delta) + user (0 if not present) + retrieval (300) = 350 input tokens billed (50 system + 300 retrieval; if system cached, only 300)
  - Output tokens: model emits final user-facing text = 350 output tokens billed

So end-to-end billed tokens (no caching):
- Total input = 170 + 350 = 520 tokens
- Total output = 40 + 350 = 390 tokens

Billing and discounts:
- We apply your negotiated input/output per-token rates to the totals above. Discounts we agree in the SOW apply to Redwood-hosted model consumption (both input and output token lines) for the hosted API.
- Connector/vendor fees: calls to a third-party retrieval service (the 300-token retrieval) may incur separate charges from that provider; those are not Redwood-hosted model charges and are excluded from Redwood discounts unless explicitly added to the SOW.

Edge cases / notes:
- If you rely heavily on tool calls where the model emits large JSON wrappers, treat those as model output and include them when modeling output-side cost.
- If you plan to reuse identical system prompts repetitively, we can model savings from prefix caching (we can run a small simulation with your sample traffic to estimate delta).
- If you expect many short-lived sessions, the 30-minute session caching TTL for hosted API may provide marginal savings; Dedicated/Private options provide more aggressive cache controls.

Monica — feel free to add anything from the SE perspective (latency vs billing tradeoffs for batching/streaming). Once we agree, we should send James a one-page note + example calc.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Pricing & Packaging | Redwood Inference

James — thanks for the patience. Karthik and Monica's notes are captured below and we've attached the draft rate card and a one-page billing note you can include in your SOW. TL;DR summary and worked example below.

TL;DR:
- Redwood bills exact integer token counts for model input and model output.
- Model-emitted function call JSON is billed as output; tool responses only billed if fed back into the model.
- We sum tokens over the billing period and apply rates; the final invoice is rounded to cents (no per-request large-bucket rounding).
- Negotiated discounts apply to Redwood-hosted model consumption only; third-party connector/provider charges are excluded unless specified.

Worked example (same numbers from your note):
- Total billed input tokens: 520
- Total billed output tokens: 390
- Example rates (for illustration only): input = $0.80 / 1K tokens; output = $1.60 / 1K tokens
  - Input cost = 520 / 1000 * $0.80 = $0.416 -> $0.42 after invoice-cent rounding
  - Output cost = 390 / 1000 * $1.60 = $0.624 -> $0.62 after rounding
  - Total = $1.04 for that session (illustrative)

Next steps:
- If you want, Monica and I can run a short prefix-caching simulation against a 2-week sample of your traffic to estimate monthly delta (likely meaningful if you reuse a stable system prompt).
- We can bake the connector cost treatment into the SOW (if you prefer us to pass connector invoices through Redwood so discounts apply, we can outline that in the commercial terms).
